name: Ahaziah of Judah
charge: Walking in the ways of the house of Ahab, his mother being his counsellor to do wickedly; going down to Jezreel to see Joram
summary: Ahaziah, Jehoram’s youngest son, reigned one year and walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, was his counsellor to do wickedly (2 Chronicles 22:1-4). He went with Joram son of Ahab to war at Ramoth-gilead and then down to Jezreel to visit him, and so came into the path of Jehu, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab (2 Chronicles 22:5-7). Jehu’s men killed him, and his mother then destroyed the seed royal (2 Chronicles 22:8-10).
offenseFull: The Arabians had killed all the elder sons, so the people of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king. He reigned one year, and his mother was Athaliah, called the daughter of Omri (2 Chronicles 22:1-2); scripture often calls a grandparent father, and the other translations make it plain that she was Omri’s granddaughter, the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel. As is the mother, so is her daughter (Ezekiel 16:44). Jezebel was a heathen, but her daughter was an Israelite with the same wicked spirit, the spirit that works through weak men.

He walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly, and after his father died the house of Ahab were his counsellors, to his destruction (2 Chronicles 22:3-4). As Jezebel stirred up Ahab, Athaliah stirred up Ahaziah. This is a warning against being ruled by the wrong counsel: instead of going to the priests and the judges, as the law set for hard matters (Deuteronomy 17:9-11), he went to his mother, and a woman with a grudge ruled a kingdom through her son. He was the son-in-law of the house of Ahab (2 Kings 8:27), a picture of the curse passed from father to son.

He walked after their counsel and went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead; the Syrians wounded Joram, who went back to Jezreel to be healed, and Ahaziah went down to see him (2 Chronicles 22:5-6; 2 Kings 8:28-29). His descent from Jehoshaphat did not make his own conduct righteous; he joined the cause of Ahab’s house at the hour its judgment was arriving.
judgmentFull: The destruction of Ahaziah was of God, by his coming to Joram, for he went out with Joram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab (2 Chronicles 22:7). Joram asked Jehu whether it was peace, and Jehu answered, what peace, so long as the whoredoms and witchcrafts of his mother Jezebel were so many? There is no peace as long as a wicked woman is in power. Joram turned and fled, crying treachery to Ahaziah, and Jehu drew his bow and shot him through the heart (2 Kings 9:22-24). Ahaziah fled by the garden house and was struck in his chariot at the going up to Gur, and died at Megiddo (2 Kings 9:27).

Jehu also found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers who served him, and killed them; they caught Ahaziah hiding in Samaria, brought him to Jehu and killed him, and buried him because he was the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. The house of Ahaziah had no power to keep the kingdom (2 Chronicles 22:8-9). The remembered faithfulness of his grandfather bought him a grave, not a deliverance, and the same hand the Most High anointed to avenge Israel on Ahab cut off the king of Judah who rode with Ahab’s son.

When Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah (2 Chronicles 22:10), killing her own grandsons, or so she thought, because her power had come through her son and she meant to rule. Back then a woman was only empowered through the man. The counsellor to do wickedly finished the ruin she had counselled, and only one child, hidden in the house of God, was left of the house of David.

text.text: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his stead: for the band of men that came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.
Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.
Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the Lord like the house of Ahab: for they were his counsellors after the death of his father to his destruction.
He walked also after their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth–gilead: and the Syrians smote Joram.

And he returned to be healed in Jezreel because of the wounds which were given him at Ramah, when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab at Jezreel, because he was sick.
And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God by coming to Joram: for when he was come, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
And it came to pass, that, when Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, and found the princes of Judah, and the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah, that ministered to Ahaziah, he slew them.

And he sought Ahaziah: and they caught him, (for he was hid in Samaria,) and brought him to Jehu: and when they had slain him, they buried him: Because, said they, he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart. So the house of Ahaziah had no power to keep still the kingdom.
But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah.
